Destinations / Spiti Valley

Spiti Valley

A cold desert of cliff-top monasteries and fossil villages

Best time: May – October. Remote with long driving days and limited medical facilities. Great for adventurous families with older kids.

Highlights

  • Key Monastery perched on a hill
  • Chandratal “Moon Lake”
  • Fossil hunting in Langza
  • World’s highest post office at Hikkim

Suggested road trips

Shimla → Kinnaur → Kaza

6 days · about 420 km. Gentle acclimatisation through apple orchards of Kinnaur, Nako lake and Tabo.

  1. Shimla → Sarahan (170 km, about 6 h): Via Narkanda’s apple orchards.
  2. Sarahan → Kalpa (110 km, about 4 h): Views of the Kinner Kailash range.
  3. Kalpa → Nako (105 km, about 4 h): Cliff roads; the Sutlej and Spiti rivers meet at Khab.
  4. Nako → Tabo (65 km, about 3 h): Thousand-year-old Tabo monastery.
  5. Tabo → Kaza (50 km, about 2 h): Stop at Dhankar on the way.
  6. Kaza → Key, Kibber & Langza (60 km, about 3 h): High villages around Kaza; back the same day.

Kaza → Chandratal → Manali

3 days · about 200 km. Rough but spectacular road over Kunzum La to the Moon Lake.

  1. Kaza → Losar (60 km, about 2.5 h)
  2. Losar → Chandratal (45 km, about 3 h): Over Kunzum La on an unpaved road. Camp at the designated sites, not at the lake shore.
  3. Chandratal → Manali (120 km, about 5 h): Batal and Gramphu, then the Atal Tunnel.

Before you go

Kaza is at about 3,800 m and Kunzum La about 4,590 m. Going up through Kinnaur (Shimla side) lets you acclimatise gradually; coming in over Kunzum from Manali is a much faster climb.

Fill up at Reckong Peo and Kaza. There’s no fuel between Kaza and Tandi over Kunzum La — about 200 km.

Narrow cliff roads in Kinnaur, and an unpaved, water-crossed stretch between Losar and Gramphu that usually opens only from mid-June to mid-October. Drive in daylight.
